summary: A lightweight, console-based application that identifies a user's location in a multi-story facility via an interactive Q&A interface and provides deterministic, step-by-step navigation to the nearest exit.
key_features: Interactive location identification via guided Q&A
State-driven logic for multi-step input handling
Extensible centralized data model for rooms and routes
achievements: Designed and implemented a state-machine architecture to manage complex multi-step user input and decision branching for precise room identification. Engineered a directed graph routing system that delivers deterministic navigation paths without relying on heavy pathfinding algorithms. Orchestrated seamless phase transitions (identification → navigation → restart) and console I/O within a single execution loop, while maintaining a zero-dependency, highly extensible codebase with clean separation of concerns.
